comments.author: elichad
comments.body:
To share with reviewers, the criteria we talked about in our original discussion:

WRITE
1. check masses against ASE defaults – if there's no difference, skip the species_mass block
2. if there are custom masses, check that all elements of the same species (standard or castep_custom_species) have the same mass
3. if there are multiple masses for a species and castep_custom_species _is not_ set, create custom species for each mass
4. if there are multiple masses for a species and castep_custom_species _is_ set, raise an error and ask the user to fix the masses
5. if castep_custom_species is set or custom masses are used, write the species_mass block with those customizations


READ
1. If species_mass block is present, update the masses of the specified species accordingly.
2. If species_mass is not present, or a species is not included in the species_mass block, use ASE defaults.

Currently there's a bit more work needed to meet all of these
comments.label_reasoning: This is a general review comment outlining criteria/requirements that are not yet fully implemented, indicating missing or incomplete specification alignment.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Outlines a detailed list of criteria that still need to be met, indicating missing functionality that should be implemented.

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body:
There's something a bit funny going on with the warning messages.

```
In [21]: import ase.build

In [22]: atoms = ase.build.molecule('CH4', vacuum=4.)

In [23]: atoms[3].mass = 2.

In [24]: atoms.write('CDH3.cell')
/home/adamjackson/opt/ase-fork/ase/io/castep.py:255: UserWarning: Warning: custom mass specified forstandard species C, creating custom species
  warnings.warn('Warning: custom mass specified for'
/home/adamjackson/opt/ase-fork/ase/io/castep.py:255: UserWarning: Warning: custom mass specified forstandard species H, creating custom species
  warnings.warn('Warning: custom mass specified for'
/home/adamjackson/opt/ase-fork/ase/io/castep.py:261: UserWarning: Warning: creating custom species H:0 with mass {2.0: [3]}
  warnings.warn('Warning: creating custom species {0} with mass {1}'.format(custom_species_name, str(mass_dict)))
```

When only changing one mass, I get a custom species warning for every species. Yet the resulting .cell file does only use one custom species.

```
#######################################################
#CASTEP cell file: CDH3.cell
#Created using the Atomic Simulation Environment (ASE)#
#######################################################

%BLOCK LATTICE_CART
 9.258236  0.000000  0.000000
 0.000000  9.258236  0.000000
 0.000000  0.000000  9.258236
%ENDBLOCK LATTICE_CART

%BLOCK POSITIONS_ABS
C  4.629118  4.629118  4.629118
H  5.258236  5.258236  5.258236
H  4.000000  4.000000  5.258236
H:0  5.258236  4.000000  4.000000
H  4.000000  5.258236  4.000000
%ENDBLOCK POSITIONS_ABS

%BLOCK SPECIES_MASS
H:0 2.0
%ENDBLOCK SPECIES_MASS
```

(Also, there should be a space in the middle of "forstandard" and we don't need to include the word "Warning:".)
comments.label_reasoning: Warning messages are incorrectly triggered for every species even when only one mass is changed, indicating a logic error in the condition for emitting warnings. Also includes a string formatting bug ('forstandard').

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Reports a bug with incorrect/excessive warning messages, a missing space in a string ('forstandard'), and suggests removing the redundant 'Warning:' prefix — all concrete fixes.

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body:
I was able to raise
`ValueError: write_cell: error writing custom masses found custom species H with inconsistent masses (2.0 and 1.008) please fix manually`

by loading a .cell file with custom species and changing a mass. As discussed I think it's good for us to bow out of interpreting this situation. The error message could however be more helpful. How about something like:

> ValueError: custom mass(es) were set, but an inconsistent set of castep_custom_species was already defined. If using both features, ensure that each species type in atoms.arrays['castep_custom_species'] has consistent mass values and that each atom with non-standard mass belongs to a custom species type.

(Try to avoid beginning an error message with e.g. "write_cell: ", as to a troubleshooter this could look like something that was produced by the stacktrace. In fact this hard-coded string can easily become outdated as things are moved and renamed.)
comments.label_reasoning: The error message is unhelpful and misleading to troubleshooters; the comment requests a clearer, more actionable error message.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests improving the error message with specific recommended wording and advises against prefixing messages with function names.

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body:
Thanks Anish, this is looking promising. We should add some tests.

Generally in ASE tests involve little reference data; they rely on generating appropriate data with ASE features and specifically checking the correctness of the functionality being tested.

So for this, I think we'll want
- Create Atoms with a custom mass (from a list of positions or using ase.build.molecule), write to .cell, check that the .cell file has a species_mass block in it with the right content.
- Read the .cell file, check that the positions and masses match the original Atoms
- Repeat the above with an existing custom species on multiple atoms being changed, ensure custom species name survives round-trip
- Repeat the above, changing e.g. _all_ Hydrogen atoms, check mass block didn't invent a new label
- Try setting a custom species on _different_ atom before write, assert error is raised (`with pytest.raises(AppropriateException): ...`).

There is an existing ase/test/calculator/castep directory, but I think ideally this would go in a new ase/test/io/test_castep.py to indicate that it doesn't involve calling the calculator. (Hopefully more CASTEP tests can live there over time...)

[ase/test/fio/text_xyz.py](https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/blob/master/ase/test/fio/test_xyz.py) is a reasonably simple/clean example of some reader tests; [ase/test/cell/test_cell.py](https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/blob/master/ase/test/cell/test_cell.py) is another clean example using a couple more Pytest features.
 `pytest` will run any function with a name beginning with `test_` and `pytest.mark.parametrize` can be used to pass parameters to repetitive tests. Bare assert statements can be used with `pytest.approx()` for many comparisons.
comments.label_reasoning: General comment requesting tests be added; primarily a documentation/coverage concern.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests multiple specific tests be added with detailed descriptions of what each test should cover and where the test file should live.

comments.author: anish-mudaraddi
comments.body:
I had a question about an edge case I found:

If we run something like:

```
atoms = ase.build.molecule('H2')
atoms[0].mass = 1
ase.io.write('new.cell', atoms)

atoms = ase.io.read('new.cell')
atoms[1].mass = 2
ase.io.write('new2.cell', atoms)
```

Do we want to produce an error? Currently we produce this output:
```
%BLOCK LATTICE_CART
 0.000000  0.000000  0.000000
 0.000000  0.000000  0.000000
 0.000000  0.000000  0.000000
%ENDBLOCK LATTICE_CART

%BLOCK POSITIONS_ABS
H:0  0.000000  0.000000  0.000000
H  0.000000  0.000000  0.250000
%ENDBLOCK POSITIONS_ABS

%BLOCK SPECIES_MASS
H:0 1.0
H 2.0
%ENDBLOCK SPECIES_MASS
```

In this case, because we have no more H with default mass, we create another label 'H' with mass as 2.0 instead of 1.008. Is this the correct thing to do?

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body:
Ooh, nice edge-case!

I suppose it would be slightly more consistent to error/complain in this case. But for practical purposes, the user has made it clear what they want and we are able to satisfy it - albeit not in the most attractive way.

It seems harmless. If we can't distinguish between "set this atomic mass to 2" and "set all remaining atomic masses to 2", and the result will be a valid calculation with the expected behaviour, I think we should err in the user's favour :wink:
